title: IT support, help desk, technical support

noc.title: User support technicians
noc.applies_when: Help desk, service desk, desktop and deskside support, end-user support. The default code for this lane.

noc.title: Computer network and web technicians
noc.applies_when: Where the body carries real network, server or infrastructure duties rather than end-user tickets. Better RCIP coverage.

noc.title: Information systems specialists
noc.applies_when: Application support and systems support seats with analysis content. Stronger code where the duties genuinely support it.

skills.name: Ticket handling and SLAs
skills.asked_for: Queue management, prioritisation, escalation, resolution within target
skills.evidence: Certify Technologies, daily. 95 percent first-contact resolution is the anchor stat for this lane.

skills.name: Active Directory
skills.asked_for: Account lifecycle, groups, permissions, password and lockout handling

skills.name: Microsoft 365 administration
skills.asked_for: Exchange Online, Teams, SharePoint and OneDrive at admin level, licensing

skills.name: Hardware support
skills.asked_for: Laptops, desktops, peripherals, printers, diagnostics and replacement

skills.name: Customer communication under pressure
skills.asked_for: Non-technical users, frustrated users, clear written updates
skills.evidence: Certify Technologies plus a year of contact centre work at Bill Gosling Outsourcing.

skills.name: Remote support tooling
skills.asked_for: Remote desktop and remote assistance tools

skills.name: Documentation and knowledge base
skills.asked_for: Writing the article so the next person does not re-solve it
skills.evidence: Repo documentation is strong; formal KB authoring in a service desk tool is not evidenced.
skills.limit: Repo documentation is strong; formal KB authoring in a service desk tool is not evidenced.

skills.name: Networking fundamentals
skills.asked_for: TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, VPN, basic switching, troubleshooting connectivity
skills.evidence: Practical troubleshooting and self-hosting setup. Not formal network administration. This is the gap between 22221 and 22220.
skills.limit: Not formal network administration. This is the gap between 22221 and 22220.

skills.name: ITSM platforms
skills.asked_for: ServiceNow, Jira Service Management, Freshservice, Zendesk
skills.evidence: Ticket workflow experience at Certify; the specific enterprise platform varies by posting, so check the named tool each time.
skills.limit: Ticket workflow experience at Certify; the specific enterprise platform varies by posting, so check the named tool each time.

skills.name: Scripting for support
skills.evidence: Strong Python and automation scripting. PowerShell specifically is not evidenced and it is the one most often named.
skills.limit: PowerShell specifically is not evidenced and it is the one most often named.

skills.name: Endpoint management
skills.note: Named often enough in mid-size employer postings to be worth closing.

skills.name: Mobile device support
skills.asked_for: iOS and Android enrolment and troubleshooting
skills.evidence: General support exposure, not MDM-managed fleets.
skills.limit: General support exposure, not MDM-managed fleets.

skills.name: CompTIA A+
skills.asked_for: Frequently listed as an asset, occasionally as a requirement. A requirement makes it a credential-gate drop

skills.name: ITIL Foundation
skills.asked_for: Same. Asset in most postings, fatal only where hard-required

skills.name: CCNA
skills.asked_for: Only matters for the 22220 network-leaning seats

skills.name: Azure or M365 administrator certification
skills.asked_for: Moves him from support into systems administration

positioning:
This is his strongest lane on paper and it should be treated that way. The 95 percent first-contact resolution figure is concrete, unusual and quotable, and it leads every application in this lane. The Bill Gosling year adds the thing most junior support candidates cannot show: a track record of holding a conversation with an unhappy person and still landing the outcome.

Most postings in this lane grade Tier A. The two gaps that recur are PowerShell and Intune or SCCM, and closing either would remove the most common named requirement he misses. Where a posting leans network rather than end-user, it is likely 22220 and likely a stretch, so name the networking gap rather than glossing it.
interview_watch: Expect a scenario: a user cannot log in, walk me through it. Answer it as a structured diagnostic, not a guess list, and say out loud when you would escalate and why. Expect a question about handling a queue when everything is urgent. The first-contact resolution number is the natural place to anchor that answer.
pr_note: This is his broadest-pathway lane. 22221 is on the Brandon RCIP list and was on Manitoba's MPNP list as of v3.1 (re-verify). 22220 is on the North Bay and Sault Ste. Marie RCIP lists. AIP covers both from a designated Atlantic employer, and Ontario's Workforce Priority stream takes either with a qualifying offer. More live routes than any other lane he has.
not_required: Security operations, firewall administration, and anything requiring a clearance. A posting hard-requiring Reliability Status or a clearance is a credential-gate drop regardless of skill.
